| M1 | Presented BRIEF-derived defaults as settled ("yes to default") with no provenance, so old-brief inferences would have passed as JJ's facts. | SEED, JJ's redo request | Wireframes built on unverified tenancy/offline/realtime assumptions. | - |
| M2 | Left out four irreversible facts: who pays, day-one integrations, scale/outage cost, vendor/budget limits. | SEED, JJ's redo request | Shapes drawn without knowing which integrations and payer flows need screens. | - |
| M3 | Treated ledger tags as labels only; JJ needs them as a gate (counts printed, invented rows asked, no advance while open). | SEED, rule from JJ | Invented calls (e.g. file layout, step order) silently becoming canon. | - |
| M4 | Auto-picked a product row (P11 reference apps) when the question gate blocked the structured question. | SEED, JJ's rule 6 | A design reference chosen by me, not JJ, shaping every session/console/artifact wireframe. | - |
| M6 | Drew the interviewee's sessions as a fixed linear count ("session 1 of 3"); JJ: a person who knows a lot gets several sessions pending at once, per topic. | WIREFRAMES J1, JJ's first review | A session engine and invite model keyed to one deck per person; the per-person queue/home would have been a retrofit across sessions, routing, and the adapt engine. | - |
| M7 | Recommended fresh-link-only recovery, forgetting that links tapped in mobile mail apps open in an in-app browser and drop the remembered device; JJ's "why not email?" made me re-derive it.
